fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. God tells Ezekiel to "…set your face toward the south, preach against it, and prophesy against the forest of the Negev." (Ezekiel 20:46) Direction AND a target. You know when your phone's map says "turn around when possible" and leaves you to figure out the rest? This is nothing like that.
Water is the opposite direction, friend. God says He will "…ignite in you a fire…" and that fire will devour all the trees. No flood anywhere in these verses.
Right. God says the fire "…will devour all your trees, both green and dry." Green ones don't get a pass. Both kinds are named, baker.
Yep. God says, "Then all people will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it will not be quenched." All people will see it, not just a few. And the One they'll see behind it is the LORD.

That's what Ezekiel says they're saying: "Is he not just telling parables?" (Ezekiel 20:49) He brings it to God right after hearing about a fire that will not be quenched. I think that kind of question would sting.

That's a serious charge, but it's not what Ezekiel reports. He says, "…they are saying of me, ‘Is he not just telling parables?’…" (Ezekiel 20:49) The word he reports is parables, and the text gives nothing beyond that.

That's the answer. When the people ask why he's groaning, Ezekiel is to say, "Because of the news that is coming." (Ezekiel 21:7) He doesn't give the details in that line. It makes you want to ask what news, doesn't it?

This one is actually true. Ezekiel says, "Every spirit will faint, and every knee will turn to water." (Ezekiel 21:7) Every knee, not a few. I think that's a heavy picture, because knees are what hold a person up.

Yes. God says, "…the sword is wielded against My people; it is against all the princes of Israel!" (Ezekiel 21:12) The princes of Israel are named right along with His people. That's why Ezekiel is told to cry out and wail.
Yes. God calls it "…a sword that slays, a sword of great slaughter closing in on every side!" (Ezekiel 21:14) Every side is the phrase the verse uses. I think that's a hard picture to sit with.
The verse doesn't say that. It calls the sword "…a sword of great slaughter closing in on every side!" (Ezekiel 21:14) Closing in on every side is the picture the text gives.

Stumble. God says, "So that their hearts may melt and many may stumble, I have appointed at all their gates a sword for slaughter." (Ezekiel 21:15) The sword is appointed at all their gates, so that hearts melt and many stumble. It's a hard verse, and it doesn't hide that.
Resting isn't in this verse, baker. The sword is appointed "So that their hearts may melt and many may stumble…" (Ezekiel 21:15) Stumble is the word the verse uses.

Yes. The message says, "Slash to the right; set your blade to the left—wherever your blade is directed." (Ezekiel 21:16) Both directions are named in the verse. Right, then left, wherever the blade is directed.
